subject: standby power
title: What If You Never Unplugged Anything?

scenes.text: What if you never unplugged anything? Most homes already live like this. They just never see the bill.
Your TV, modem, game console and microwave clock keep drawing power when they're off, 24 hours a day.
Across 70,000 California homes, that idle draw averaged 164 watts per home, all day, every day.
That was nearly a quarter of each home's electricity, used by things nobody was using.
It added up to about 165 dollars a year per home, and up to 440 dollars on high electricity rates.
Across America, about 19 billion dollars a year. The output of roughly 50 large power plants, just to keep things asleep.

description:
What if you never unplugged anything? An NRDC study of 70,000 northern California homes found always-on devices drew an average of 164 watts, nearly a quarter of household electricity.
That idle load costs about $165 a year per home, up to $440 on high rates, and about $19 billion a year across the US, the output of 50 large power plants.
